content: Unified memory allocation limits matter because the CPU and high-performance GPU share a single pool of system RAM, meaning they must compete for the same capacity. If the GPU is allocated too much memory for textures or shaders, the CPU may run out of space for system tasks, leading to performance bottlenecks or application crashes. Conversely, insufficient allocation to the GPU can severely throttle graphics performance, preventing the APU from utilizing its full processing potential.
